items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I sat in his big band one time and they had Sunny Murray and it was a great, great experience with Butch Morris doing conduction

ctx.x: Yeah I think that, I don’t think I’m the best person to answer that because I’m from San Francisco, I’m not part of like the New York scene. So in some ways it might come off kind of detached. But my initial feelings and it’s probably not even well thought out, is that David Murray is like, I think represents that last generation, the eighties. And I just remember one year when, I think it was 1990 or maybe it was the late eighties, there was a young saxophonist, Christopher Holliday, and he was sort of — maybe…

musicians like I sat in his big band one time and they had Sunny Murray and it was a great, great experience with Butch Morris doing conduction. And so he has these ties. But I don’t know if there is that kind of mentor relationship now.
Well we certainly have the universities to teach jazz. Maybe the mentor thing has been replaced by that, by all the programs.
